open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_resolution after a not_applied resolution
open_points.text: the element is not reached any more, so the advance reaches it again through `effects.reach_operation_element`
open_points.question: Does `continue_after_resolution` merely record the resolution and enter the ordinary advance loop, or does it itself reach the resolved element before that loop? The phrase says both that it is not reached and that it is reached again, while A11 rule 3 still says the kernel reaches it in the owner's same request.
options: Only the ordinary advance loop reaches it
`continue_after_resolution` reaches it directly and then advances
A distinct resolution step marks it ready before the advance loop reaches it
open_points.default_guess: Record the resolution, then let the ordinary advance loop select and reach the element.

open_points.subject: conclusion of an operation element after not_applied
open_points.text: an operation element whose wait no longer holds (its approval decided, its attempt resolved `not_applied`) is not reached and so is ready
open_points.question: What must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return after an `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution's attempt is resolved `not_applied`, before a fresh approval has been requested? A11 rule 3 calls it waiting for `owner_approval`, while the changed recovery text calls it not reached and ready, and the public conclusion API permits `not reached` only when no NodeExecution exists.
options: Not reached and ready
Waiting for owner approval despite there being no requested approval yet
A separate ready-for-fresh-approval conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct ready-for-fresh-approval conclusion that makes the ordinary advance loop call `reach_operation_element`.

open_points.subject: recovery of a decided approval
open_points.text: an element whose approval was decided ... is not reached and so is ready
open_points.question: Does “approval was decided” mean only `approved`, or also `refused`? A refused approval already has a `refused_by_owner` NodeExecution and must end the run rather than make the element ready.
options: Only an approved decision makes an otherwise unconcluded element ready
Both approved and refused decisions make it ready
Any existing conclusion takes precedence, so only a decided approval without a conclusion is ready
open_points.default_guess: An existing conclusion takes precedence; in practice only an approved decision without a concluding NodeExecution becomes ready.

open_points.subject: sandbox_runner.read_runner_report malformed input result
open_points.text: an unreadable or partial report is not decoded into outputs
open_points.question: What does `read_runner_report` return when the channel bound is exceeded or the report is unreadable or partial? Its Outputs list has no malformed-report result and its Errors section says none, yet `sandbox` needs an explicit result to classify the execution.
options: A decoded-report result with a malformed or incomplete variant
A synthetic escaped-exception result
An internal error
No result, with `sandbox` inferring failure from process state
open_points.default_guess: Return an explicit malformed-or-incomplete report variant that `sandbox` classifies as `crashed`.

open_points.subject: run_values.assemble_mapped_lists value-list output
open_points.text: Every list built — a value list as the StoredValue of the canonical array of the elements' values ... Observable effect: None; nothing is written.
open_points.question: What exactly represents a value list before it is written? A StoredValue M21 is a stored record with a `value_id`, but this operation writes nothing, so callers cannot know whether they receive a draft record, canonical bytes and facts, or an already valid reference.
options: An unwritten StoredValue draft including its computed identity and bytes
Canonical bytes, schema and class from which delivery later creates the StoredValue
An opaque derived-source descriptor consumed only by `deliver_input` or `record_flow_output`
open_points.default_guess: Return an opaque derived-source descriptor containing the canonical bytes and StoredValue facts, which is converted to a stored reference on delivery.

open_points.subject: mapped file-list references
open_points.text: the reference to a mapped node's file list; the empty lists of a mapped node over an empty list, built for the node's own record
open_points.question: What model value or reference represents a mapped file list, especially an empty one, and where is its disclosure class carried? M23 names files through individual SpooledFile facts, while an empty list has no SpooledFile from which its class or identity can be recovered.
options: An inline ordered file-list reference carrying its class
A new stored file-list record
A NodeExecution output field with a separately stored list class
No reference, deriving both membership and class from other inputs each time
open_points.default_guess: Use an inline ordered file-list reference that carries its disclosure class and may contain zero SpooledFile identities.

open_points.subject: run_graph.plan_run result precedence
open_points.text: the `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` records that became determined, as drafts ...; the next ready node with its elements and the source of each input
open_points.question: May one `plan_run` result contain both new drafts and a ready node, and if so must `runs` write the drafts before executing that node, execute first, or treat such a result as invalid? The choice changes trace/store order and recovery behavior.
options: Drafts and a ready node may coexist; write drafts and re-plan before execution
Drafts and a ready node may coexist; execute the node before writing drafts
The result must expose either drafts or a ready node, never both
open_points.default_guess: Return drafts before executable work; `runs` writes them and re-plans before executing a node.

open_points.subject: run_values.record_flow_output source contract
open_points.text: The source of one produced flow output and the actor.
open_points.question: Which source variants may `record_flow_output` receive, and what must it do for each? The text does not say whether it accepts only a mapped-list draft, the same three-way source union as `deliver_input`, or an already-written StoredValue reference as well.
options: Only an unwritten mapped value-list source
The same source union as `deliver_input`
Either an existing StoredValue reference or an unwritten mapped value-list source
open_points.default_guess: Accept either an existing StoredValue reference or an unwritten mapped value-list source, writing only the latter.
